target.title: fix(googlechat): add timeout to Google auth fetch requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Google Chat auth requests made through `createGoogleAuthFetch()` — the shared fetch implementation injected into Gaxios as the Google auth transport — had no request deadline. Token refresh, cert fetch, and any other HTTP auth operation could wait indefinitely when a Google auth endpoint accepted the connection but never responded.

## Why This Change Was Made

A 30s request timeout (`GOOGLE_AUTH_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`) is added to the single `fetchWithSsrFGuard` call inside `createGoogleAuthFetch()`. This brings Google Chat auth fetches in line with every other OAuth/token path in the codebase:

- Chutes OAuth token exchange (#102026): 30s
- MiniMax OAuth (#102862): 30s  
- Google Vertex ADC token refresh (#102050): 30s
- Google Chat cert fetch in `auth.ts` (#102924): 30s
- QQ Bot token (#102897): 30s
- Mattermost REST (#102027): 30s

The existing SSRF policy, dispatcher routing, body-size limit (1 MB), response buffering, and release lifecycle are unchanged.

## User Impact

A stalled Google auth HTTP request now aborts within 30 seconds through the existing `fetchWithSsrFGuard` timeout infrastructure instead of leaving the Google Chat integration stuck indefinitely.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/googlechat/src/google-auth.runtime.test.ts` — 21 tests passed.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/googlechat/src/google-auth.runtime.ts extensions/googlechat/src/google-auth.runtime.test.ts` — clean.
- The focused regression test uses a real `node:http` loopback server that accepts the auth fetch without responding, and proves the request rejects with an `AbortError`/`TimeoutError` within the deadline.
- No open PR touches `google-auth.runtime.ts`; `auth.ts` (PR #102924) is a separate file covering a different call site.
